terms.meaning: The number of digits after the decimal point. 5.96 has 2 decimal places.
A decimal that never ends, because a block of digits repeats. 1 ÷ 3 = 0.333…
A year with 366 days. It is needed because the Earth takes about 365.2422 days to go around the Sun.

items.name: Dividing by 10, 100 or 1000
items.formula: Move the point 1, 2 or 3 places left

items.name: Multiplying by 10, 100 or 1000
items.formula: Move the point 1, 2 or 3 places right

items.name: Placing the point
items.formula: Decimal places in the answer = the places in both numbers added

items.name: Both numbers more than 1
items.formula: The product is more than both

items.name: Both numbers between 0 and 1
items.formula: The product is less than both

items.name: One of each
items.formula: The product lies between the two numbers

items.name: Fractions that end
items.formula: Denominators with only 2s and 5s give decimals that end

items.name: Dividing by a decimal
items.formula: Multiply both numbers by a power of 10

items.name: The leap year rule
items.formula: Divisible by 4, but not by 100, unless also by 400
items.example: 2024 and 2000 are leap years, but 1900 is not.

items.name: Why the rule is needed
items.formula: Each year is 0.2422 days longer than 365
items.example: In 100 years the calendar slips by 0.2422 × 100 = 24.22 days.

mistakes.text: Multiplying by 10 moves the point right, and dividing moves it left. 2.5 × 10 = 25, and 2.5 ÷ 10 = 0.25.
Multiplying by a decimal below 1 makes a number smaller. 8 × 0.5 = 4.
A year divisible by 100 is a leap year only if it is also divisible by 400. 1900 was not a leap year.
